feed.title: Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs

entry.title: Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs
entry.summary:
The email discusses technical aspects of blockchain technology, specifically focusing on the use of a language model to draft text and the classification of blockchain transactions based on security and exposure levels. The sender clarifies that although a language model assisted in drafting the email, the content itself is derived from real-world data classifications and not solely generated by the machine. These classifications include scenarios such as truncated indexer history and specific API blind spots like the P2PK issue.
The email further delves into the updates made to the system, referencing version 0.2.0 revisions which were prompted by the discovery of actual vulnerabilities during reviews. It also mentions test vectors that can be independently verified, emphasizing the practical application and verification of the data provided.
Moreover, the discussion explores the necessity for different levels of transaction classification at various stages or conditions within the blockchain, such as per-output levels at a certain block height or a committed set. This granularity helps determine whether script-level or outpoint-level profiles are required for accurate transaction classification. The dialogue also touches upon the potential addition of a node-level exposure index to enhance the existing models without presupposing any specific indexing.
In terms of semantics, the sender acknowledges a discrepancy between what data indicates and how it's interpreted or used, suggesting that the current draft might benefit from explicitly stating these differences. They propose refining the classification labels to better reflect the actual risk associated with transaction spendability versus the provability needed for future recovery actions, illustrating this point with examples from current consensus rules and proposed standards like BIP341.
Lastly, the sender agrees to integrate feedback into the next version update (v0.3.0), considering suggestions for renaming certain classifications to avoid misinterpretation, such as changing 'EXPOSED_ON_SPEND' to 'EXPOSED_WHEN_SPENT', which more accurately describes the condition under which key material becomes public.
